title: A proper scheme of dimension at most one over a field is projective
statement: Let $k$ be a field and let $X$ be a proper scheme over $k$ with topological Krull dimension $\dim X\leq1$ (with $\dim\varnothing=-\infty$; for nonempty $X$, the dimension is that of [def-pc-dimension]). Then there are an integer $N\geq0$ and a closed immersion $X\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^N_k$ over $k$; equivalently, $X$ is projective over $k$ ([def-pc-projective-morphism]).

proof.text: The proper structure morphism $X\to\operatorname{Spec}(k)$ is separated and of finite type by the definition of properness. Since $\dim X\leq1$, the dimension-one quasi-projectivity lemma [lem-sc-dim-one-quasi-projective] gives an integer $N$ and an immersion $i:X\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^N_k$.

source.place: Lemma 0A26 proof, first sentence, invoking Lemma 0A25 (lines 9217-9222)

proof.text: The structure morphism $\mathbf P^N_k\to\operatorname{Spec}(k)$ is separated [lem-weil-pbc-projective-space-proj-separated]. Thus $i$ is proper by the proper-over-separated lemma [lem-weil-pbc-proper-over-separated], because its composite with the structure morphism is the proper morphism $X\to\operatorname{Spec}(k)$. The image $i(X)$ is therefore closed by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-closed-image]. Finally, an immersion with closed image is a closed immersion by [lem-weil-pbc-immersion-closed-image-closed-immersion], so $X\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^N_k$ is a closed immersion and hence projective by [def-pc-projective-morphism].
